result:
**Mechanism:** Decode is memory-bandwidth-bound. Each step reads all the weights plus every sequence's KV cache.

- **Weights:** 70.6B parameters in BF16 is about 141 GB.
- **KV cache:** 80 layers × 8 KV heads × 128 dim × 2 (K and V) × 2 bytes is 320 KB per token. At 8192 tokens that is about 2.7 GB per sequence.
- **Bandwidth:** B300 has about 8 TB/s HBM, and I assume about 85% is achievable, so roughly 6.8 TB/s.
- **Step time:** bytes read per GPU divided by effective bandwidth, plus about 160 small all-reduces per step over NVLink at TP>1 (roughly 2–3 ms), plus about 1 ms of overhead.
- **Per-GPU throughput:** batch × per-user rate ÷ TP.

Candidates, with approximate numbers:

| TP | Batch | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 32 | About 227 GB read per step gives about 28 tok/s per user. Fails the 30 tok/s floor. |
| 1 | 8 | About 40 tok/s per user, about 320 tok/s per GPU. |
| 2 | 32 | About 800 tok/s per GPU. |
| 2 | 128 | About 242 GB per GPU per step, about 26 tok/s per user. Fails. |
| 4 | 128 | About 121 GB per GPU per step, about 21 ms, about 47 tok/s per user, about 1500 tok/s per GPU. |
| 4 | 256 | About 207 GB per GPU per step, about 29 tok/s per user. Marginal miss. |
| 8 | 256 | About 103 GB per GPU per step, about 15 ms of reads plus about 3.5 ms of comms and overhead, about 19 ms, about 53 tok/s per user, about 1700 tok/s per GPU. |

TP8 at batch 256 splits both weights and KV cache eight ways, so it clears the 30 tok/s floor with margin. It also gives the highest per-GPU throughput, about 1,700 tok/s. TP4 at batch 256 would be higher if it passed, but my estimate puts it just under 30 tok/s per user.
